fixes.explanation: That's it, baker! Moses and Aaron carry a message to Pharaoh, and they tell him what the LORD says: "But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow." (Exodus 10:4) Notice the word tomorrow. The warning comes with a day attached. Pharaoh has a chance to humble himself before then.

Nope, baker, Pharaoh's daughter doesn't show up in this scene at all. The text says Pharaoh's officials ask him, "How long will this man be a snare to us?" (Exodus 10:7) So his own officials are the ones who speak up. They've watched Egypt take hit after hit, and I think they've run out of patience.

It's True, friend, and I love that you're checking. Pharaoh's officials tell him, "Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God." (Exodus 10:7) Then they hit him with, "Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?" (Exodus 10:7) Even the people standing closest to Pharaoh are saying it. I think they were done waiting for him to catch up.

That's the one, baker. Pharaoh asks who exactly will be going (Exodus 10:8), and Moses answers, "We will go with our young and old. We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD." (Exodus 10:9) He doesn't trim the list at all. Young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds, all of them are going to worship.

You got it, baker. Pharaoh has just said that the day Moses sees his face again, he will die. Moses answers, "As you say… I will never see your face again." (Exodus 10:29) He agrees, and the meeting is over. I think that's a heavy way for this scene to end.
